tests.title: A change made on one side only is taken as it stands
given: a base tree and two sides, where one side changes a file, adds a file and deletes a file and the other changes nothing
tests.when: the three-way merge is computed
then: the merged tree carries the changed file's new content and mode
the added file is present and the deleted file absent
no conflict is reported
tests.pseudocode: in the three-way merge test file: t = merge(base, ours, theirs); assert entry(t, 'a') == entry(ours, 'a') and 'new' in t and 'gone' not in t

tests.title: Identical changes on both sides merge cleanly
given: a base tree and two sides that make byte-identical changes to the same file, and identical additions and deletions
tests.when: the three-way merge is computed
then: the merged tree carries that content
no conflict is reported
tests.pseudocode: in the three-way merge test file: assert merge(base, s, s).tree == s.tree and no conflict

tests.title: Differing changes to one region conflict and write nothing
given: a base tree and two sides that change the same lines of one file differently, and a case where one side deletes a file the other changed
tests.when: the three-way merge is computed for each
then: each reports a conflict naming the path
no tree object is produced
a second file both sides left alone is not named
tests.pseudocode: in the three-way merge test file, table over the conflicting shapes asserting conflict.paths == [p] and no tree

tests.title: Renames, modes, deletions, additions and binary files behave as git does
given: for each shape, a base and two sides built identically for the engine and for a real git repository
tests.when: the merge is computed by the engine and by the real git binary
then: for each shape, the merged tree or the conflict matches git's
binary files are not line-merged by either
a mode change on one side alone survives the merge
tests.pseudocode: in the merge differential test file, table over the five shapes comparing engine and git results

tests.title: A clean merge does not depend on the order of its sides
given: the three-way merge over generated base and side trees
tests.when: for generated inputs that merge cleanly, the merge is computed with the sides in both orders
then: both orders produce the same tree object id
neither order reports a conflict where the other does not
tests.pseudocode: in the three-way merge test file, a generative test: assert merge(b, x, y).tree == merge(b, y, x).tree for clean cases

tests.title: A rebase copies every commit of the branch, in order, onto the base
given: a base with two commits and a branch with three of its own commits
tests.when: the branch is rebased onto the base
then: the resulting history holds exactly three new commits
their order matches the branch's original order
the base's two commits are behind them
tests.pseudocode: in the rebase test file: h = rebase(branch, base); assert [c.message for c in own(h)] == [c.message for c in own(branch)]

tests.title: A copied commit keeps its author and message and takes new parents
given: a branch whose commits have distinct authors, messages and timestamps
tests.when: it is rebased onto a base
then: each copied commit's author and message equal the original's
each copied commit's parent is the previous copy, or the base for the first
each copied commit's id differs from the original's
tests.pseudocode: in the rebase test file: for orig, copy in zip(branch, result): assert copy.author == orig.author and copy.message == orig.message and copy.id != orig.id

tests.title: A commit already present in the base is handled as git handles it
given: a branch containing a commit whose changes the base already has, built identically for the engine and for a real git repository
tests.when: the rebase is run by the engine and by the real git binary
then: the two resulting histories are identical in tree, parents and commit count
whatever git does with the empty commit, the engine does the same
tests.pseudocode: in the rebase differential test file: assert history(engine_rebase()) == history(git_rebase())

tests.title: A rebase conflict stops at that commit and applies none after it
given: a branch of three commits whose second conflicts with the base
tests.when: the branch is rebased onto the base
then: the result is a conflict naming the paths and the commit it stopped at
no object from the third commit is reachable from any ref
the repository's refs are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the rebase test file: r = rebase(branch, base); assert r.conflict.at == branch[1].id and refs() == before

tests.title: A merge produces one commit with two parents in the right order
given: a base and a branch that diverge from a common ancestor and do not conflict
tests.when: the branch is merged into the base
then: exactly one new commit is produced
its parents are the base's head first and the branch's head second
tests.pseudocode: in the merge strategy test file: c = merge_commit(base, branch); assert c.parents == [base.head, branch.head]

tests.title: The merge commit's tree equals git's
given: base and branch histories built identically for the engine and for a real git repository, including a case with a criss-cross merge base
tests.when: the merge is computed by the engine and by the real git binary
then: the two merge commits have the same tree object id
that holds for the criss-cross case as well as the simple one
tests.pseudocode: in the merge differential test file: assert engine_merge().tree == git_merge().tree

tests.title: A conflicting merge produces no commit
given: a base and a branch that change the same region differently
tests.when: the merge is attempted
then: no commit or tree object is written
the conflict names every conflicting path
the repository's refs are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the merge strategy test file: r = merge_commit(base, branch); assert r.conflict and objects_written() == 0

tests.title: The conflicting path set equals git's
given: cases with one conflicting path, several conflicting paths, and conflicting paths alongside cleanly merged ones, built identically for both implementations
tests.when: each is run by the engine and by the real git binary
then: the two path sets are equal for every case
no cleanly merged path appears in either set
tests.pseudocode: in the conflict differential test file: assert set(engine.conflicts) == set(git.conflicts)

tests.title: A conflict's identity is stable across occurrences and distinct between conflicts
given: one conflict reproduced twice from the same content, and two conflicts differing only in one side's content
tests.when: the identity is computed for each, before and after a restart of the process
then: the two occurrences of the same conflict yield equal identities
the two different conflicts yield different identities
the identity is unchanged after the restart
tests.pseudocode: in the conflict identity test file: assert id(c1) == id(c1prime) and id(c1) != id(c2)

tests.title: A conflicting operation leaves the repository untouched
given: a repository with a known ref list, and a rebase and a merge that each conflict
tests.when: each operation is run to its conflict
then: the ref list and every ref's target are unchanged afterwards
no object written during the attempt is reachable from any ref
tests.pseudocode: in the engine integration test file: before = refs(); run_conflicting(); assert refs() == before and unreachable(written)

tests.title: Resolving a conflict records the resolution against its identity
given: a conflict and a resolution for it
tests.when: the resolution is recorded and the resolutions are listed
then: an entry exists for that identity
its resolved flag is true
tests.pseudocode: in the recorded resolutions test file: record(id, res); assert entry(id).resolved is True

tests.title: A recorded resolution is replayed and the operation continues
given: a patch that conflicts with a base, and the resolution recorded for that conflict
tests.when: the same patch is applied to the same base again
then: no conflict is reported
the operation completes
its result equals the result of applying the resolution by hand
tests.pseudocode: in the recorded resolutions integration test file: record(id, res); r = apply(patch, base); assert not r.conflict and r.tree == manual.tree

tests.title: A recorded resolution outlives the process that recorded it
given: a resolution recorded for a conflict
tests.when: every component but the store is restarted and the same conflict is reached again
then: the resolution is applied
the operation completes without reporting the conflict
tests.pseudocode: in the recorded resolutions integration test file: record(); restart(); assert not apply().conflict

tests.title: Resolutions are listed with their identity, path, time and resolved flag
given: one conflict that has been seen but not resolved, one resolved while its path was known, and one resolved from an earlier run with no known path
tests.when: the resolutions are listed
then: each entry carries an identity and a recorded time
resolved is true only for the two with a resolution
path is present where it is known and absent otherwise
tests.pseudocode: in the recorded resolutions test file: entries = list(); assert [e.resolved for e in entries] == [False, True, True] and entries[2].path is None

tests.title: A resolution is forgotten by identity, or by path while in conflict
given: two recorded resolutions, one for a path currently in conflict
tests.when: one is forgotten by identity, the other by path, and a third forget names a path that is not in conflict
then: each forgotten entry is gone from the listing and its conflict is reported again next time
the forget naming a path that is not in conflict removes nothing and says so
tests.pseudocode: in the recorded resolutions test file: forget_by_id(a); forget_by_path(b); assert a not in list() and b not in list(); assert forget_by_path(c).removed == 0

tests.title: Over the generated corpus the engine's history equals git's
given: the generated corpus and a real git binary
tests.when: each case is run through the engine and through git with the same strategy
then: the resulting tree object id is identical for every case
each commit's parent list is identical
the commit order is identical
a case that differs in any of the three fails the run
tests.pseudocode: in the differential suite: for case in corpus: e = engine.run(case); g = git.run(case); assert (e.tree, e.parents, e.order) == (g.tree, g.parents, g.order)

tests.title: Over the generated corpus the engine's conflicts equal git's
given: the generated corpus and a real git binary
tests.when: each case is run through both
then: a case conflicts for the engine exactly when it conflicts for git
for every conflicting case the two path sets are equal
tests.pseudocode: in the differential suite: assert bool(e.conflict) == bool(g.conflict) and set(e.paths) == set(g.paths)

tests.title: The corpus covers the named shapes at the stated size
given: the corpus generator
tests.when: a corpus is generated and its cases are classified
then: the corpus holds at least 200 cases
at least one case exists for each of linear history, branching history, renames, binary files, mode changes, empty commits, merge commits in the source, conflicting patches and clean patches
at least one case applies a stack of 20 or more patches
tests.pseudocode: in the corpus generator's test file: c = generate(); assert len(c) >= 200 and SHAPES <= {case.shape for case in c} and max(case.stackSize) >= 20

tests.title: A fifty-patch stack applies at the stated repository size
given: a repository of 500 MB of packed objects and a stack of 50 patches, each within 1000 changed files and 10 MB of diff
tests.when: the stack is applied
then: the operation completes
the resulting history matches git's for the same inputs
tests.pseudocode: in the engine size integration test file, skipping with a named reason when the fixture cannot be built: assert apply_stack(50).completed and matches_git()

tests.title: An operation past a stated limit fails and names it
given: inputs exceeding the patch count, the repository size, the changed-file count and the diff size in turn
tests.when: each operation is attempted
then: each fails rather than stalling
each failure names which limit was exceeded
no operation runs past the platform's limits or is killed
tests.pseudocode: in the engine limits test file, table over the four limits asserting the failure and the named limit

tests.title: An operation too large for one unit of work continues in another
given: a stack whose application cannot finish within one unit of platform work
tests.when: it is applied to completion
then: the operation completes
it was continued at least once rather than restarted
its result equals the result of the same operation run within one unit
tests.pseudocode: in the engine integration test file: r = apply_large(); assert r.completed and r.continuations >= 1 and r.tree == reference.tree

tests.title: An abandoned operation leaves the repository unchanged
given: a repository with a known ref list and a long operation
tests.when: the operation is abandoned part way, and separately fails part way
then: the ref list and every ref's target are unchanged in both cases
no partial result is reachable from any ref
tests.pseudocode: in the engine integration test file: before = refs(); abandon(op); assert refs() == before

tests.title: The engine works against both repository store implementations
given: the engine and both implementations of the repository store
tests.when: a rebase, a merge and a replayed resolution are run against each
then: every operation succeeds against both
the results are identical
the engine reaches no store API directly
tests.pseudocode: in the engine integration test file: for store in [artifacts(), local()]: assert rebase(store).tree == expected

tests.title: The engine runs with no git binary on the path
given: an environment with no git executable
tests.when: a three-way merge, a rebase, a merge commit and a replayed resolution are run
then: every operation succeeds
no operation attempts to start an external process
tests.pseudocode: in the engine integration test file, with PATH stripped of git: assert all operations succeed

tests.title: A branch is rebased in a real repository and the new head reads back
given: a real repository store holding a workspace repository with a base and a branch
tests.when: the engine rebases the branch onto the base and the new head is read back through the store
then: the new head carries the branch's commits in order with the base's history behind them
the objects were read and written through the repository store
the operation ran with no git binary present
tests.pseudocode: in the engine smoke test file: head = engine.rebase(ws, branch, base); assert history(store.read(head)) == expected

tests.title: A resolution recorded before a restart is replayed after it
given: a real repository store, a patch that conflicts with a base, and the resolution recorded for that conflict
tests.when: every component but the store is restarted and the patch is applied to the same base again
then: the engine recognises the conflict by its identity
the recorded resolution is applied
the operation completes without reporting a conflict
tests.pseudocode: in the engine smoke test file: record(); restart(); r = engine.apply(patch, base); assert not r.conflict

tests.title: The whole corpus agrees with the real git binary
given: a generated corpus of at least 200 cases and a real git binary
tests.when: the differential suite runs every case through both implementations
then: every case agrees in tree, parents, commit order and conflicting paths
the suite reports the number of cases it compared
the suite skips with a named reason when no git binary is available
tests.pseudocode: in the differential suite's entry point: report = run_corpus(); assert report.mismatches == 0 and report.compared >= 200
